answer:
Yes, there are several things to raise. The most important is your stool test. Your fecal immunochemical test (FIT) on 4 November 2025 was positive. A positive FIT means you need a diagnostic colonoscopy to find the cause. Nothing in your records up to 15 October 2026 shows that this was done or booked. If it happened somewhere else, make sure your doctor has the result. If not, book it now.

Your diabetes checks look overdue. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026, about eight and a half months ago. Your metformin is marked as ended on 15 April 2024, and the records give no reason. Empagliflozin (Jardiance) was prescribed on 20 February 2025. Ask whether you are taking it and what your diabetes plan is now. Your A1c peaked at 8.3% in January 2025 and has come down since.

Your cholesterol was high on 18 February 2025 (LDL 131 mg/dL). That test was done two days before atorvastatin was prescribed, and there is no repeat cholesterol test in your records.

Your kidney function is still in the normal range (eGFR 69 in February 2026, down from 73 a year earlier). I do not see a urine albumin test in the past year, which is usually part of yearly diabetes care. I also do not see a diabetic eye exam. These may have been done elsewhere.

One item that looks like a problem but is not: your pulmonary embolism entry is marked as ruled out, and the CT scan on 8 July 2025 showed no PE. You may still want to ask about the high D-dimer blood test from that day.

This is based only on the records I have and general guidance. Your doctor has the full picture.
short: Positive stool test (FIT) on 4 Nov 2025 with no follow-up colonoscopy in my records; last A1c 6.9% on 16 Feb 2026, now overdue; LDL 131 before starting a statin, with no repeat lipid panel.

items.says: The pulmonary embolism entry is marked as ruled out, and the CT scan on 8 July 2025 showed no PE. Nothing is open here, though you may want to ask about the high D-dimer blood test from that day.
items.why: A negative CT angiogram is the definitive test for a clot in the lungs. A D-dimer is sensitive but not specific, so a high result alone does not mean a clot.
